transcript:
This is "NPR News Now," the latest headlines every hour.
Live from "NPR News" in Washington, I'm Louise Schiavone.
Israel's president says he has tapped Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's main rival,
Gadi Isincott, to form the new Israeli government.
Neither Netanyahu nor Isincott won a clear majority in last month's election.
And PR's Lauren Freire reports from Tel Aviv.
Prime Minister Netanyahu's party won slightly more seats than Gadi Isincott's.
But leaders of most of Israel's other parties have recommended Isincott be tasked with forming
a government rather than Netanyahu, who is Israel's longest-serving prime minister.
A statement from Israeli President Isaac Herzog's office says he'll hold a ceremony with Isincott
on Sunday evening local time.
Isincott is a former military chief whose son was an Israeli soldier killed in combat in
Gaza.
He'll have about six weeks to try to form a coalition government, after which, if he's
unsuccessful, Herzog would ask someone else.
And if that person can't form a coalition, Israel could face fresh elections.
Lauren Freire, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
In the aftermath of the midterm elections, blue sweep, there has been a change in the
Trump White House.
Chief of Staff Susie Wiles is out and longtime Trump strategist and insider Stephen Miller
is the new chief of staff.
At the Conservative Heritage Foundation, President Kevin Roberts calls us a good move.
What it signals to not just the radical left majority coming into Congress, but for all
of us on the political right, that President Trump and his administration are not rolling
over.
I know that people who are on the political left disagree, maybe with Stephen Miller with
everything, they probably disagree with me in heritage with everything.
He's an extremely competent, politically conservative, very intellectual policymaker.
And for those of us on the political right who are charting the way forward after this
week's major defeat, I think Stephen's a perfect choice.
Roberts spoke with NPR's All Things Considered.
Federal law enforcement officials have given little indication that they are investigating
the deaths of nine people who have been killed by ICE agents.
NPR's Meg Anderson reports the killings will likely be a focus when the new Congress convenes
next January.
Once they have a majority in Congress, Democrats say they plan to issue subpoenas to major
players in Trump's mass deportation plan, compelling them to answer key questions under
oath.
That could include Homeland Security Secretary Mark Wayne Mullen and his predecessor Kristi
Noem, among others.
Brent Ganger is the brother of Renee Good, a U.S. citizen killed by an ICE officer in
Minneapolis last January.
He says hearing more about his sister's death will be hard.
But I think it's also super important for us to understand what happened that day.
In a statement, DHS told NPR that Democrats are, quote, "more interested in political
shenanigans than in governing," but said the agency is prepared.
Meg Anderson, NPR News.
From Washington, you're listening to NPR News.
Poland's Interior Minister Marcin Kerewinski says the gunman who today opened fire in Krakow's
busy main square was a Polish citizen with very radical and ultra-nationalistic views.
Six people are dead, 15 people were injured.
Police say the 25-year-old man wore military fatigues and used an automatic rifle targeting
random people as he drove through the area.
Poland's defense minister has called it an act of terror.
The nation's organ transplant system has adopted emergency rules to improve the safety
of a new controversial form of organ procurement, and PR's Rob Stein has that story.
The Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network's board of directors approved new
rules for a type of organ donation known as NRP.
The procedure involves restarting circulation quickly after a potential donor has been declared
dead because their heart stopped.
NRP was developed to obtain more organs for transplants, but critics say the procedure
violates the fundamental rules for how donors are declared dead.
The new policy was developed after concerning reports of blood flow, possibly returning
to the brains of NRP donors after they were declared dead.
The new policy could be revised after the public has a chance to weigh in.
Rob Stein, NPR News.
The Christmas tree destined to grace the front of New York City's Rockefeller Center arrives
in Manhattan today, the 76-foot Norway spruce traveled from West Edmondston, New York, wrapped
in over 50,000 LED lights.
I'm Louise Schiavone, NPR News, Washington.

topics.text: Israeli President Herzog taps rival Gadi Isincott to try forming new government
Stephen Miller named Trump White House chief of staff after Susie Wiles departs
Democrats plan subpoenas over nine deaths from ICE agent shootings, including Renee Good
Gunman kills six in Krakow main square; Poland calls attack an act of terror
Organ transplant network adopts emergency rules for controversial NRP organ procurement procedure
76-foot Norway spruce arrives in Manhattan for Rockefeller Center Christmas tree
